slot.brief: Order given species by bond angle or bond length (e.g., NO2+/NO2/NO2– or NH3/PH3 series) using hybridisation/lone-pair logic

stem: Arrange $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_4$ in increasing order of bond angle.

verdicts.working: Bond angles: H₂O ≈ 104.5°, NH₃ ≈ 107°, CH₄ = 109.5°. Thus H₂O < NH₃ < CH₄.

working:
Lone-pair repulsion reduces bond angles: $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($2$ lone pairs) $< \text{NH}_3$ ($1$ lone pair) $< \text{CH}_4$ (no lone pairs).

Independent check: Bond angles: H₂O ≈ 104.5°, NH₃ ≈ 107°, CH₄ = 109.5°. Thus H₂O < NH₃ < CH₄.
solution:
Lone-pair repulsion reduces bond angles; more lone pairs cause greater compression.
$\text{H}_2\text{O}$ has two lone pairs, $\text{NH}_3$ has one, and $\text{CH}_4$ has none.
Thus, increasing bond angle: $\text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{NH}_3 < \text{CH}_4$.
